association.limitations: NASA's detailed record and primary paper establish the instrument and observation date of the corresponding plume product. ESA's NIRCam wording remains a recorded source conflict. The separate Cassini inset's exact observation epoch remains unverified. NASA PNG and ESA JPEG are distinct publisher renditions; visual correspondence does not establish byte or pixel preservation. Monochrome infrared water emission assigned blue is not calibrated visible colour or resolved surface geography.

paper.title: JWST molecular mapping and characterization of Enceladus’ water plume feeding its torus
paper.copyPublicationDate: Author-hosted copy contains an unresolved online-publication placeholder; no exact publication date inferred from that placeholder.
paper.rights: Exclusive publisher agreement and US Government-work notice with possible foreign protection; no CC BY assertion. Research-only PDF; no figure embedded.
paper.findings: Trailing-hemisphere observations on 9 November 2022, NIRSpec IFU program 1250. Primary extent wording is 40 Enceladus radii; retain publisher radius/size wording differences. Rotational excitation 25±3 K is not ambient kinetic gas temperature. Column density and outgassing are model-derived, not direct local surface composition. Non-detections do not establish absence; tentative molecular assignments remain tentative.
